preamble: Backing of the velar fricative [x] to the uvular fricative [χ] happens next to open or back vowels. In Standard German, the ach-Laut is uvular [χ] after /a, aː/ but velar after /uː, oː/. In Castilian Spanish the velar fricative /x/ can be pronounced uvular before a back vowel or [w], as in junio [ˈχunjo] 'June' (Martínez-Celdrán et al. 2003).

examples.note: The ach-Laut is uvular [χ] after /a, aː/ but velar [x] after /uː, oː/ (Buch [buːx] 'book').
Martínez-Celdrán et al. (2003) describe /x/ as velar, but say it can be pronounced uvular before a back vowel and the semivowel [w].
The preceding nasal assimilates to the uvular fricative.

sources: Martínez-Celdrán, E., Fernández-Planas, A. M., & Carrera-Sabaté, J. (2003). Castilian Spanish. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 33(2), 255–259. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100303001373
